nodes.content: Design an SSD-backed key-value store that limits write amplification under long-lived snapshots without sacrificing crash consistency.
requirements: Reduce total host-written bytes by 30% versus leveled LSM compaction under identical update-heavy workloads.
Preserve snapshot isolation and acknowledged writes across crashes; keep p99 reads within 10% of baseline.

nodes.content: Use an fsynced WAL and indexed MVCC runs; park snapshot-pinned versions in immutable segments while compacting unpinned updates.
How can indexed pinned segments keep p99 point-read latency within 10% of leveled LSM as snapshots accumulate?
An epoch-aware per-key version index keeps p99 point reads ≤1.10× leveled LSM with 32 long-lived snapshots.
Benchmark epoch-indexed segments against leveled LSM under 32 eight-hour snapshots, tracking p99 point-read latency and host-written bytes.
Run SnapMix-32 comparing epoch-indexed segments with leveled LSM under 32 eight-hour snapshots; record p99 reads and host-written bytes.
SnapMix-32 measured 2.14 ms p99 point reads versus leveled LSM's 2.00 ms, with 32% fewer host-written bytes.
Run SnapMix-Sweep at 1, 8, 32, and 64 eight-hour snapshots, comparing indexed-segment and leveled-LSM p99 point reads.
SnapMix-Sweep at 32 snapshots with an 8 GiB cache measured 2.42 ms p99 versus leveled LSM’s 2.00 ms.
Does epoch-index metadata eviction explain SnapMix-Sweep’s 2.42 ms p99 point reads under an 8 GiB cache?
With resident epoch-index metadata, 32 snapshots meet ≤1.10× baseline p99; 8 GiB cache eviction causes additional SSD reads.
Reproduce SnapMix’s 2.14/2.42 ms p99 runs; compare index evictions, SSD reads, and p99 before and after metadata pinning.
At 8 GiB, pinning epoch metadata eliminated index evictions and lowered p99 point reads from 2.42 to 2.16 ms.
Pin epoch-index metadata at 32 snapshots; its measured 2.16 ms p99 stays within 10% of the 2.00 ms baseline.
Separate values into an append-only log; use a WAL-backed version index and reclaim records only after snapshot expiration.
Which value-log and WAL flush order prevents acknowledged writes from referencing missing values after power loss?
Fdatasync value-log records before their WAL index entries, then fsync WAL before acknowledgment to prevent dangling recovered pointers.
Run 10,000 CrashCut power-failure injections before and after value-log fdatasync and WAL fsync; verify acknowledged writes and pointers.
CrashCut’s 10,000 injected failures recovered every acknowledged write with zero dangling value-log pointers.
Use CrashCut-Rotate to inject power loss around log-segment creation and WAL commit, checking directory persistence and acknowledged value recovery.
CrashCut-Rotate found 7/2,000 failures where acknowledged WAL pointers survived but newly created value-log segments vanished without directory fsync.
When must the value-log directory be fsynced relative to segment creation and WAL commit to preserve acknowledged writes?
Fsyncing the value-log directory after segment creation, then fdatasyncing records before WAL fsync, eliminates dangling acknowledged pointers.
Repeat CrashCut and CrashCut-Rotate with/without post-creation directory fsync; inject failures around value fdatasync and WAL fsync, verifying acknowledged writes.
CrashCut-Rotate confirmed value-before-WAL syncing on stable segments, but 3/10,000 acknowledged pointers referenced missing renamed segments despite creation-time directory fsync.
Run 10,000 CrashCut-Rename injections, comparing creation-only and post-rename directory fsync with value-before-WAL syncing and acknowledged-pointer recovery.
CrashCut-Rename lost 3/10,000 acknowledged segments with creation-only directory fsync, versus zero with post-rename fsync and value-before-WAL ordering.
Fsync value-log directories after segment creation or rename; fdatasync values before WAL fsync, then acknowledge to prevent dangling pointers.
Use epoch-pinned page-map roots and append-only B-tree deltas, consolidating at eight versions with checksum-verified atomic root commits.
How does eight-version consolidation affect host-written bytes and p99 reads when 32 snapshots pin distinct page-map roots?
On SnapMix-32, eight-version consolidation reduces host-written bytes ≥30% versus leveled LSM while keeping p99 reads ≤2.20 ms.
Run SnapMix-32 with 4-, 8-, and 16-version consolidation, comparing host-written bytes and p99 reads against leveled LSM.
SnapMix-32 eight-version consolidation wrote 34% fewer host bytes than leveled LSM; p99 reads were 2.17 versus 2.00 ms.
Keep eight-version consolidation for pinned-root B-tree deltas; SnapMix-32 met both byte-write and p99-read targets.
Use WAL-durable, copy-on-write hash buckets with snapshot-pinned bucket generations and bounded version-chain indexes to avoid rewriting cold values.
What bucket size balances copy-on-write rewrite bytes against p99 lookup latency under 32 snapshots and 1% hot-key skew?
Sweep 4–64 KiB buckets on SnapMix-32 with 1% hot-key skew, measuring host-written bytes and p99 point reads.
Run SnapMix-32 at 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64 KiB buckets; compare write bytes and p99 reads with leveled LSM.
SnapMix-32 bucket-sweep report contains per-size host-written bytes and p99 point-read latency versus leveled LSM under 1% hot-key skew.
Analyze SnapMix-32 report for bucket sizes meeting ≥30% host-byte savings and ≤2.20 ms p99; inspect pinned-generation lookup costs.
Across SnapMix-32 bucket sizes, maximum host-byte savings were 22%, while minimum p99 was 2.31 ms versus 2.00 ms.
Reject copy-on-write hash buckets: no tested size met either ≥30% host-byte savings or ≤2.20 ms p99.
Use indexed first-write snapshot preimage overlays; WAL-durable records let leveled compaction discard pinned versions without losing snapshots.
How can overlapping snapshots share preimage records without duplicating writes or exposing later values during reads?
Index each preimage by its visibility sequence interval; overlapping snapshots within that interval share one WAL-durable record.
Compare interval-indexed preimages with SnapMix-32 B-tree/hash controls under overlapping snapshots; measure sharing, isolation violations, host bytes, and p99.
SnapMix-32 shared 2.8 snapshots/preimage, recorded zero isolation violations, saved 39% host bytes versus LSM, and reached 2.13 ms p99.
Adopt visibility-interval preimage sharing: SnapMix-32 saved 39% host bytes, held p99 at 2.13 ms, and showed zero isolation violations.
